title: Config safety linter + stepwise rewind: automated rollback with state snapshots and cost-aware triggers
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: config changes to batching, caching, kernel selection and routing can unexpectedly increase cost or degrade SLOs. We need an automated rollback system that is cost-aware, can detect regressions quickly, and reliably reconcile system state after a rollback (including KV cache, batching configuration, and routing tables).

Proposal: implement a three-part system: 1) pre-apply safety linter and simulated dry-run that flags high-risk changes and produces a cost/regression delta estimate; 2) runtime triggers that detect KPI regression (latency, error-rate, cost-per-token, tail-latency) and initiate stepwise rewind (canary revert -> partial revert -> full revert) with guardrails and hysteresis; 3) state snapshot & reconciliation service that captures safe checkpoints for rollback (config + minimal runtime state) and performs idempotent reconciliation to avoid split-brain after partial rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Safety linter runs on every config change and blocks or requires approval for changes with estimated cost delta > 10% or tail-latency risk > 20%
Dry-run simulator produces token-cost and latency delta estimates for a given traffic profile and stores results in the change audit
Runtime triggers detect regression conditions and automatically start a stepwise rewind with proper audit logs
Snapshot store can capture and restore minimal runtime state required for safe rollback (routing configs, batching thresholds, cache priming keys) within SLO
Reconciliation service verifies post-rollback state matches snapshot and retries idempotently if differences are detected
Feature is gated behind a runtime feature flag and rolled out to 1%->10%->100% with metric dashboards for each stage
Unit and integration tests cover simulated dry-run, trigger evaluation, rollback execution path, and reconciliation success/failure paths
implementation_notes: Components: config-service (validation + linter), change-simulator (offline cost/latency model), rollback-orchestrator (state machine), snapshot-store (S3 + metadata), reconcile-engine (idempotent patcher), observability hooks (dashboards + alerting)
Add new telemetry metrics: config_apply_cost_delta, config_apply_latency_delta_p95, rollback_initiated_by, rollback_phase, reconcile_attempts
Use existing runtime-apply API but add a 'dry_run' mode that runs compilation/kernel-selection heuristics on representative seq-length distributions
Snapshot size must be bounded: only store config + small index of cache priming keys. Do not snapshot whole KV cache. Document expected restore time and acceptable staleness.
Design linter rules as configurable policies: cost_threshold_percent, latency_threshold_percent, dependency_whitelist, canary_required
Guardrails: minimum canary window, minimum traffic to apply change, maximum concurrent rollbacks per cluster to avoid cascade
testing_plan: Unit tests for linter rule evaluation and dry-run estimator (coverage > 90%)
Integration test in staging that runs a synthetic workload generator and applies a high-cost change to verify automatic stepwise rewind triggers
Chaos test: induce partial network partition during rollback to validate reconcile-engine idempotency
Load test: snapshot/restore under peak QPS to measure restore latency and effect on serving nodes
Postmortem drills: run simulated incident and document recovery runbook
rollout_plan: Feature flag default OFF for all customers
Internal dogfood cluster -> enable for runtime-team only (1%)
Beta: enable for non-critical customer tenants (10%) with manual monitoring
Gradual increase to 100% after 2 successful weeks and product sign-off
Keep quick opt-out toggle and emergency global rollback handler in Console for first 30 days post-GA
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives in linter block harmless changes -> Mitigation: provide override with explicit approver and show dry-run evidence
Risk: snapshot/restore adds latency during rollback -> Mitigation: only restore minimal items and rely on lazy cache warm-up
Risk: cascading rollbacks across clusters -> Mitigation: global concurrency cap and staggered unwind windows
Risk: cost-model divergence from real-world -> Mitigation: continuously calibrate model with weekly A/B data and store historical deltas
